method: Text without language: fleet-fable's published drifting line chain (the lines and first_lines of R-017, experiments/R-attack-F-018/fleet-fable/attack.json, word for word, fitted on public training pages only), with its ordinary lines written out in two interleaved passes: first every odd-numbered line of the chain's output, then every even-numbered one; paragraph-opening lines unchanged. As published, the chain overshoots F-021 (0.051 on the practice split, bound 0.045) because its one-glyph copies of the last 15 words land on the line directly above. Interleaving puts each line next to one written two lines later in the chain, so the altered copies stay near but mostly off the previous line: practice value 0.017, inside 0.012 to 0.045, against the manuscript's 0.030. Disclosure, as the red team requires: three orderings were tried on the practice split with this fact in view (pairs of lines swapped 0.020 but failing the shuffle null; two-way interleave 0.017 passing; three-way interleave -0.006 failing), and this is the one that passed; no rule names a glyph, a word or the line above, but the ordering was chosen against the fact, so a second look may fairly call it weak. What it shows if it holds on the hidden pages: F-021's band is reachable by a meaningless copy-and-vary procedure once its altered copies are kept off adjacent lines, which is the property F-021 describes, not evidence of language. fleet-opus registered F-021 and attacks it here.
